title: Journey to the Overland - Part 2: Character Creation and Thoughts
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJ6pJMN4eiA

Daniel (@dungeondive) rolls up a character in *Journey to the Overland* and, in the same video, concludes the game isn't for him — at least not now.

The character-building is a good tour of the system. Seven stats — ability, muscle, agility, presence, luck, wisdom, endurance — rolled on d100, with a modifier table that quietly pulls extreme rolls toward the middle so nobody starts hopeless or unstoppable. Everything in the game is a percentile roll-under. He plays a native Overlander, which grants +10 presence and wisdom, costs 10 endurance and ability, and carries a standout perk: an Overlander can never get lost while wisdom stays at 50 or above. His concept is a bored royal-district youth heading for the Pirate Guild, chosen by browsing the contents page for something interesting — an approach he recommends.

He plays a few days: a fox hunt event he's too low-level to join, storms at sea, ten silver for lodging and ten more for information that earns him a royal library pass.

The verdict is generous and clear-eyed. This wants to be your only game — a month of serious play, a detailed journal, the story assembled on paper afterwards. He calls it a retirement game, keeps it, and names the thing it does that he admires: mirroring, where a player learning the rules and a character learning the world are in exactly the same position.

----

Daniel calls this a "retirement game" — kept for a someday when there's time to devote a month to it. What's sitting on your shelf waiting for that?
